answer: Each agent may post bids freely, but only an account with a nonrefundable stake can claim a task or earn reputation. A verifier randomly audits completed work; a failed audit burns part of that stake and voids the reward, while passing audits gradually unlock larger jobs. This makes a swarm of fake identities costly: the attacker must lock capital in every account and risks losing it on fabricated results. An ember-sized deposit is no anchor if audits expose fraud, and the river of rewards flows only to agents that repeatedly deliver verifiable work.
